default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-148.title: Deep-book micro-break fade
E-148.hypothesis: When the last hour's price impact (range per contract traded) is well below its 20-session norm, the book is deep and liquidity providers absorb small pushes; a close beyond the last 5 minutes' high/low in such a regime is a small order moving through refilled quotes and reverts, so fade it.

E-149.title: Double-sided sweep, follow the second break
E-149.hypothesis: A break of the recent high soon followed by a close below the recent low has run the stops on both sides; the first-side breakout buyers are now trapped and liquidating together with the fresh breakdown sellers, so the second break carries; follow it (mirror).

E-150.title: Volatility-decay retracement after a storm
E-150.hypothesis: A 30-minute burst of abnormal activity with a directional move, followed by a quiet stretch at half the storm's pace, means the forced flow is done and the market makers who took the other side now hold inventory they lean back on; once the calm sets in, trade against the storm's move.

E-151.title: Close-to-close vs range variance ratio trend follow
E-151.hypothesis: When close-to-close variance rises above the Parkinson range variance of the same bars, bars are closing near their extremes instead of rotating inside them: a one-sided order is lifting each bar's close; the crossing of that ratio marks persistent flow, so follow the window's direction.

E-152.title: Yesterday's closing-hour push reversal
E-152.hypothesis: A last hour that moved much more than usual is closing-benchmark and rebalancing flow, not information; the inventory dealers took on at the close is unwound in the next morning, so in the first part of today's session trade counter bars against yesterday's closing-hour push.

E-153.title: Previous clock-hour overreaction fade
E-153.hypothesis: A completed clock hour that moved far more than a typical hour attracted hourly-chart chasers at its close; in the first minutes of the next hour the first bar closing beyond the previous bar against that hour shows the chasers are not being followed, and their exits revert the overreaction; fade the hour.

E-154.title: Momentum re-acceleration follow
E-154.hypothesis: In a move larger than usual for its horizon, a slowdown of the short-term speed WITHOUT a pullback that is followed by a renewed speed-up shows the parent order resumed after a pause rather than meeting supply; a re-accelerating move still has an active initiator, so follow it (mirror).

E-155.title: Leverage-effect asymmetry fade
E-155.hypothesis: In an equity index, volatility normally rises when price falls and fades when it rises; an up move with rising volatility is a short squeeze of forced buyers, and a down move with falling volatility is orderly selling with no fear behind it; both lack the usual participants, so fade them.

E-156.title: Post-wide-day consolidation fade
E-156.hypothesis: After a session whose range was much wider than the 20-session average, day traders cut size and dealers rebuild inventory; the next session tends to consolidate inside the shock, so short-term breaks of the recent high/low are not followed and are faded on that next day only.

E-157.title: Bollinger-inside-Keltner squeeze release
E-157.hypothesis: When the close-based standard deviation band sits inside the range-based Keltner channel, closes are pinned while bars still trade (two-sided absorption); the first bar where the bands expand back out is when one side stops absorbing, and the many squeeze-indicator users enter with the momentum; follow the side of the close relative to the mean.
